title: Heusch, Hattorf and the Elector Georg Ludwig to Jobst Hermann von Ilten, 1705-1706, code B, GWLB Hannover Ms XXIII 1245:7 (catalogue 346)

steps.what: Kalliope SRU search 'Ilten dechiffriert': six items; the record notes read 'Dechiffrierter Brief' (deciphered), not 'not deciphered' as the catalogue had it.
Found Parts IV and VII of the Receuil de Lettres a J. H. d'Ilten in the GWLB Kitodo library (POST search), mapped folios to physical images through the METS files, fetched the 17 leaves.
Transcribed letters B, C, D: clear text, 418 code groups and the interlinear glosses, from crops of the master images.
Built a table of every group with every gloss it carries (tables.py): no contradictions; code B shared by the French and German letters; 91 identified as a null.
Read letters B-D from the glosses: the Prussian marriage of Sophia Dorothea (1705-06). 7 groups left unglossed by the interliner.

Split under the one-key rule from ilten1697: letters B, C, D (code B) get their own entry, with ciphertext_B/C/D.txt, letter_D_1706.txt and the B-C transcription; tables.py rerun on code B alone (418 groups, 215 distinct, 7 unglossed).

outcome.method_basis: Every code run of the three letters carries a contemporary interlinear decipherment, 7 groups apart; the work transcribed it and checked it against the recurrence of each group.
outcome.fraction_read_source: ciphertext_B-D.txt: 418 code groups; 7 unglossed (B 419; C 709, 276, 78?, 626, 728, 36?) counted unread; 91 counted read as a null

gaps.item: groups running into the binding at the right margin (glosses legible)

outcome.notes: Catalogue premise corrected: Kalliope's 'Dechiffrierter Brief' means deciphered; the sender of D is Georg Ludwig, not Georg Wilhelm. No key for code B. Split on 14 Oct 2026 from ilten1697 (code A).

credits.note: interlinear decipherments on every code run (recipient's office)

prior.where: Interlinear decipherments on the letters themselves (GWLB); Kalliope notes 'Dechiffrierter Brief' on each record.

human: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and posed the problem with /goal, pasting the catalogue entry. No target-specific intervention recorded.
